body:
CONFIRMED AGAINST CURRENT SOURCE AND RUNTIME — C2 BLOCKER, PLAN ITSELF IS CORRECT.

The permutation amendment is necessary. In `acquire/.../resolve.scala:335-352`, `collect` assigns each distinct value its first-appearance index and both `resolve` and `alternatives` use that index as the final tie-breaker. The existing property named "resolution is deterministic" only evaluates the same bundle twice; it does not permute the proposal multiset.

I ran the current `acquireJVM/Test/console` with two distinct ordinary-family proposals having identical provider count, proposal count, raw score 0.9, calibrated probability 0.95, and valid span support:

  forward = Accepted(1, 0.95, evidence e1)
  reverse = Accepted(2, 0.95, evidence e2)
  equal   = false

So asynchronous completion order can change both the accepted scientific value and accepted evidence while every substantive input remains the same. This is stronger than an output-order cosmetic defect.

The repair should not merely replace arrival order with an arbitrary lexical or hash winner. For two distinct candidates tied on all declared decision evidence, acceptance has no scientific basis: return `Alternatives`. Give that alternative set a canonical serialized order using a stable typed candidate identity/content digest. Add a permutation property over the complete proposal multiset plus the exact two-way tie court above. This keeps the plan commitment that resolution is permutation-invariant without manufacturing certainty from a deterministic but semantically irrelevant key.

No shared files changed; this was a read-only source/runtime check.
